sections.html: Priapella chamulae is a quite rare livebearer. Like Priapella intermedia, it has brilliant blue eyes. It is a medium-sized species and reaches about 6 cm in length.
Priapella are schooling fish that live near the surface in brooks.

Priapella are specialized fish. Conditions such as keeping in schools (10 specimens or more), good current and oxygen-rich water have to be imitated in the aquarium, otherwise one will have only little fun with Priapella.
Priapella are schooling fish. They should be kept in schools of 10 specimens or more.
Lexicon: Priapella: ancient Greek, means "small penis". chamulae: after the indigenous tribe of the Chamula, which live in the region in Mexico where the species is found.
